body:
**Working entry (chk-p27sjwqs):** Error text in the answer — `caused` carries each record's message from every
source, framework and engine beside the app, scrubbed and bounded; whether every error boundary can be read, measured
first.

**Purpose (the founder's, set with his answer):** an agent driving a headless harness reads, from an acting answer
alone, what failed and where, and can go after the problem — not only that something failed. [inferred] — the
founder's own answer and purpose, relayed from `~/dev/projects/additional/escher-overseer/relays/error-text-founder-2026-11-16.md`
(snapped after the promotion, cited here by its `inputs#I{n}`).

- An acting answer's `caused` (`click` · `type` · `press` · `advance` · `scroll`; `packages/escher-driver/src/caused.rs`,
  built by 2026-11-16-errors-with-the-action as closed words, ids and counts alone) gains the TEXT of what the step
  caused, per record, from every source:
  - a **panic**: its payload and its source location (file, line, column), as the panic hook already reads them
    (`packages/escher-telemetry/src/panic.rs`);
  - an **error** the app's root error boundary took: its message AND its cause chain (each `source()` in turn), not
    its top line alone — today `RootErrorMark` (`packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/boundary.rs`) holds the error by
    identity and reads nothing of it;
  - a **log record** from the app, the UI framework and the engine: its message, its target (which source said it),
    its level, the location a bridged `log` record carries (`log.file` · `log.line`) and its fields — today the
    capture (`packages/escher-telemetry/src/capture.rs`) counts records by level alone and admits no engine or escher
    target.

- **The scrub** — every field of every record passes the scrub by field name that already stands on the log sink
  (`packages/escher-telemetry/src/format.rs`: the content field names, the engine's safe-field rule); a field the
  scrub hides is shown hidden (its name and the redaction marker), and the rest of the message still crosses — a
  message is never blanked because one field in it is. The ratified mask is unmoved: a password's or a file input's
  value never crosses.

- **The bounds, set by measurement** — each message cut at a fixed length; an answer carries at most a fixed count
  of records; both numbers are set from the lengths research measures, so that the usual message arrives whole.
  A cut is never silent: a cut message says it was cut and by how much; the records past the count are counted, by
  source.

- **Every carrier** — the text rides `caused` wherever `caused` rides today: the in-process `Outcome`, the command
  line's JSON line, the session socket's `call`, an MCP tool result and a kept check (recorded, replayed, its answer
  kept whole); the MCP result bound (1,048,576 bytes) and the socket answer bound hold over it.

- **The help** — `describe()`'s self-description names the new fields of `caused` and the cut's and the count's
  meanings.

data.head: ## Measured first (research, before the bound is set)

body:
- **Real message lengths** on the stand and fixtures: a panic with its location, an error with its source chain,
  the engine's and the framework's records an acting step causes on the stand's tasks — the distribution read, and
  the cut and the count set from it. [inferred]

- **Whether every error boundary can be read**: the app's own error boundaries (an `ErrorBoundary` component inside
  the app) as well as the root one — whether the error an app's own boundary catches can be read by the driver at
  all, and with what; the result states what is read and what is not, and an unread boundary is said by the tool's
  own help, never silent. [inferred] — the CARRY's «an error an app's own boundary catches is measured for whether it
  can be read».

- On a fixture with a **real failure** (a handler that fails the way an app fails — a panic in a real code path, an
  `Err` with a cause chain, a framework or engine record), an agent reading **the answer alone** can say what failed
  and where: the acceptance asserts the message, the source location and the cause chain are in the answer, not only
  that the fields are present.
- The scrub: a record with a secret-named field crosses with that field hidden and the rest of its text whole.
- The bounds: a message past the cut arrives cut with the cut said; records past the count are counted by source.
- Both layout modes; in process, through the command line and over MCP.
- Not taken: the whole unscrubbed text, and the scrub with no cut (the founder passed both over).

- No new verb, carrier, exit, refusal cause, session error, socket or listener. The log sink's own lines are
  unchanged: no message, payload or field value reaches a log line or a span field that does not already (the
  `command` and `tool_call` spans keep their fixed fields; the text crosses only as the command's answer).

- Error text is page- and app-authored content crossing onto the ratified carriers: a boundary widening inside the
  founder's answer, owed its security-plan and architecture amendments at the wrap.

- CARRY `cry-jboglltk` (whole): «the founder's own answer to 2026-11-16-errors-with-the-action's F1 — the error's

  reading, not his words: each record's message, each field through the sink's own scrub, each message cut at a fixed

body:
# The founder's answer on «Error text in the answer» — 2026-11-16

The founder answered one question by question dialog in the overseer session on 2026-11-16; the answer was read at
15:47Z. It is his own chosen label, verbatim; the overseer relays it.

## What of an error's text crosses onto an answer's `caused`

> «Скраб и граница (Recommended)»

The option as it was read to him: the message of every record from every source — the app, the framework and the
engine; every field passes the same scrub by field name that already stands on the log sink (the values of fields
such as a password or a token are hidden); each message is cut at a fixed length; an answer carries a fixed count of
records and the rest are only counted. Its stated price: a long error arrives cut, and the value of a field with a
secret name is not shown to the agent even where a diagnosis would want it. The ratified crossing (a password's and a
file input's value do not cross the socket) stays as it is.

Passed over, as they were read to him:
- the whole text, unscrubbed — every field value as written, a boundary widening by his word, the route entry's
  «scrub held» lifted and the security masters rewritten;
- the scrub kept with no cut — messages uncut and the count of records per answer unbounded.

## The purpose he set for it, typed by him right after the answer, verbatim

> «Надо так чтоб агент понял ошибку и смог разобраться в проблеме, мы строим хедлесс харнесс для него»

The overseer's reading, read back to him in the overseer session and confirmed by him, typed, verbatim: «Все верно» —
how the chosen option is built to that purpose:
- the bound is sized by measurement, not picked: the phase reads the lengths of real messages (a panic with its
  location, an error with its source chain, the engine's and the framework's records on the stand) and sets the cut
  so that the usual message arrives whole;
- a cut is never silent: a cut message says it was cut and by how much, and the records past the count are counted
  by source;
- what an agent needs to find the problem rides with the text: where it happened (the source location a panic or a
  record carries), which source said it, and the error's cause chain, not its top line alone;
- the scrub hides a value by its field's name and nothing else: a message is not blanked because one field in it is;
- the chunk's acceptance asks the question he asks — can an agent, from the answer alone, say what failed and where —
  on a fixture with a real failure, not only that the fields are present.

This confirms the reading of his typed words of the morning (`morning-answers-founder-2026-11-16.md`, item 2): the
text of every source, scrubbed and bounded.

title: The measurement (before the bound is set)

data.head: ## The measurement (before the bound is set)

body:
A temporary probe target `tests/blitz-tests/tests/zz_probe_error_text.rs` (its source kept at
`{work_dir}/evidence/zz_probe_error_text.rs.txt`, removed from the tree after the reading) drove every
actionable control of the four lean tasks, Cells' first three cells (click, `=sum(A0:A3)`, Enter) and the load
page through the harness, and a real-failure fixture, under a recorder subscriber that kept every event's target,
level, message and fields, a chaining panic hook that kept each payload and location, and reads of the root
boundary's and of every registered boundary's error. 39 steps. Two builds:
`cargo test -p blitz-tests --locked --features dioxus-native-dom/tracing --test zz_probe_error_text -- --nocapture`
(the engine's `tracing` on, as the workspace build compiles it; log `{work_dir}/evidence/probe-tracing.log`) and the
same without the feature (the package-alone build; `{work_dir}/evidence/probe-package.log`). Summarised by
`summarize_probe.py` (scratchpad) over each log.
**Records by source and level, message bytes (min · p50 · p95 · max), engine `tracing` on:**
| source (target crate) | level | count | message bytes |
| engine `blitz_dom::document` | INFO | 20 | 26 · 26 · 26 · 26 — `Focussed node NodeId(21v1)`, one per focus move |
| engine `dioxus_native_dom::mutation_writer` | DEBUG | 104 | 17 · 74 · 83 · 95 — attribute writes holding the attribute's VALUE as typed (`name:value, value:Some("ab12")`) and `NodeId` text |
| framework `dioxus_core` | TRACE | 614 | 17 · 19 · 523 · 4106 — the 4106 a `Debug` dump; a `self` field up to 819 B |
| framework `dioxus_signals` | TRACE | 257 | 82 · 107 · 124 · 124 |
| framework `warnings` | TRACE | 403 | 133 each |
| app (the fixture's handler) | WARN | 1 | 40 — `booking rejected: 4 seats over the limit`, fields `seats` (1 B) and `password` (7 B) |

Package-alone build: the two engine rows are absent (0 records); the framework rows read the same; the app row the
same. **At `warn` and above, no stand step caused any record under either build** — the only warn-or-above record
of the 39 steps is the fixture's own. Records per step: max 253 at every level (Crud typing), at `info` and above
max 2.

**Panics (fixture, both builds):** `index out of bounds: the len is 0 but the index is 3` — payload 52 B, location
`tests/blitz-tests/tests/zz_probe_error_text.rs:306:22` (53 B); `called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value:
ParseIntError { kind: InvalidDigit }` — payload 81 B, the location the caller's line (std's `#[track_caller]`).
A location inside a registry dependency is an absolute host path (read on the recorder's metadata: every
`dioxus_core` record's file is `/home/…/.cargo/registry/src/…/dioxus-core-0.7.10/src/runtime.rs`).

**Errors with a cause chain (fixture, both builds):** a handler `Err` built from a three-link chain
(`LoadError` → `SettingsError` → `ParseIntError`): top line 31 B, `{:#}` form 97 B, the chain 3 links / 93 B, read by
`CapturedError`'s `Deref` to `anyhow::Error` and its `chain()` — no new dependency.

**The bound the measurement supports:** the longest message of an admitted class (an app record at any level, a
framework or engine record at `warn` and above, a panic, a boundary error's link) read 97 B, and at most 2 such
records crossed a step. A per-text cut of 1024 bytes holds the longest measured ten times over; a count of 16
records per answer holds the largest measured step eight times over.

title: Whether every error boundary can be read (measured)

data.head: ## Whether every error boundary can be read (measured)

body:
- **The root boundary:** yes — `ErrorContext` at `ScopeId::ROOT_ERROR_BOUNDARY`, as `root_error_mark` already reaches
  it (`packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/boundary.rs:35`); its error read whole with its chain.

- **A boundary of the app's own (`ErrorBoundary { … }`):** yes, through dioxus-core's own hook
  `provide_create_error_boundary(fn() -> ErrorContext)` (re-exported at `dioxus_core`, `#[doc(hidden)]`): every
  `ErrorBoundary` built under a scope that provides it takes its `ErrorContext` from that factory
  (`dioxus-core-0.7.10/src/error_boundary.rs:68-77`), so the factory can register each one. Measured twice:
  provided from the app's root component (1 context registered at boot; the own boundary's error read after the
  click, 3 links, its fallback rendered), and provided by the document's side at `ScopeId::ROOT` through
  `VirtualDom::in_scope` before the first build, with no app code (2 contexts registered at boot — the root error
  boundary's and the app's own; after the click the own one holds the error, the root holds none).

- **What stays unread:** an app that provides its own factory (fullstack's hydration factory) shadows the document's
  for the scopes under it — stated by the tool, never silent; and an error stays in its boundary after the step, so
  a new one is told by identity before and after the step, as `RootErrorMark` already does.

- `packages/escher-driver/src/caused.rs` (full) — `Caused` is closed words, ids and a count per kind and level; `caused()` builds a `panic` item from a count, an `error` item from the root mark, `log` items per level from `Captured`

- `packages/escher-driver/src/execute.rs` (690-760) — `settled_step` reads the root mark before, runs step and settle under `escher_telemetry::capture`, counts panics through `catch_unwind` and drops each payload
- `packages/escher-driver/src/json.rs` (340-380, 600-720) — `with_caused` / `caused_item` write the items by hand; the unit tests' `every_caused` table
- `packages/escher-driver/src/schema.rs` (165-185, 250-335) — the `CAUSED` field spec, kind `Entries`, its help ending «no message or payload», on the five acting verbs
- `packages/escher-driver/src/explore.rs` (200-215) — an exploration reads a `panic` item as its `Panicked` ending

- `packages/escher-telemetry/src/capture.rs` (full) — the scoped capture: a thread-local stack of level counts, `counted()` admitting no engine or escher target and the framework at `warn` and above, `capture()` routing through a process-wide dispatcher pair where the default holds no `CaptureLayer`
- `packages/escher-telemetry/src/format.rs` (1-130) — the scrub: `ENGINE_TARGET_PREFIXES`, `ESCHER_TARGET_PREFIXES`, `SAFE_FIELDS`, `CONTENT_FIELDS`, `REDACTED`, the private `decide()`
- `packages/escher-telemetry/src/panic.rs` (full) — the binaries' chaining hook emits `escher_telemetry::panic` with `panic.file` · `panic.line` · `panic.column` · `panic.payload`
- `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/boundary.rs` (full) — `RootErrorMark` holds the root error by identity and reads nothing of it
- `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/dioxus_document.rs` (107) — `DioxusDocument::new`, where a document-side root context can be provided before the first build, as the reached record and the seed are
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_errors.rs` (full) — the standing check asserts no payload or message byte in `caused` (`holds_no_sentinel`) on every carrier: the assertions this chunk reverses
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/fixtures/mod.rs` (15-30) — `boot`, `hold` over the stand's options

- `dioxus-core-0.7.10/src/error_boundary.rs` (60-200), `render_error.rs` (60-140), `runtime.rs` (555-580) — `ErrorContext`, `CapturedError(Arc<anyhow::Error>)` and its `Deref`, `throw_error`'s own `tracing::error!` when no boundary stands
- `examples/seven_guis/tests/common/mod.rs` — the log checks' needle helpers (`Needles`, `occurrences`), where an error-text needle class belongs

Query: `refs` for `Caused`, `CausedKind`, `CausedLevel`, `StepReading`, `root_error_mark`, `RootErrorMark`, `Captured`,
`capture` (trace `{run_dir}/tree-query-2026-11-16-error-text-in-the-answer.json`).
- **`Caused`** — referenced in `caused.rs`, `execute.rs:57,73,91,710`, `json.rs:355-714`, `lib.rs:190` (re-export) and `stand_act_errors.rs` — its shape change reaches exactly these
- **`CausedKind`** — also `explore.rs:23,210` (the `Panicked` ending) and `json.rs`' tests
- **`root_error_mark` / `RootErrorMark`** — `boundary.rs`, `lib.rs:41`, `caused.rs:104,114`, `execute.rs:712`, `stand_act_errors.rs:271,283`

- **Marker:** 2026-11-16-error-text-in-the-answer · **Version:** escher-0.3.0 · **Generated:** 2026-11-16T17:41:55Z

An acting answer's `caused` stops being closed words and counts alone. It carries, per record, the text an agent
needs to say what failed and where, and to go after it (the founder's purpose, inputs#I1). Each item says:
- a panic's payload and location;
- an error's message and its whole cause chain, and which boundary took it (the root one or one of the app's own);
- a log record's message, its source, target, level, location and fields.

It does this for every source: the app at every level, and the UI framework and the engine at `warn` and above. Every
field passes the log sink's own scrub by field name. Each text is cut at a fixed length that says how much it cut. An
answer holds a fixed count of items, and the rest are counted by kind and source (inputs#I1: «Скраб и граница
(Recommended)» and its five confirmed points).
The bounds are set from the P3 measurement (`doc:2026-11-16-error-text-in-the-answer/research` §The measurement):
- **Cut:** 1024 bytes per text. The longest admitted message measured was 97 B.
- **Count:** 16 items per answer. At most 2 admitted records crossed a step.

The text rides every carrier `caused` already rides (arch · contract/acting-verb-results/caused,
security · decision/caused-answer-crossing). It reaches no log line or span field (security ·
decision/no-screen-content-in-logs, arch · contract/command-span/never-fielded). It adds no verb, carrier, exit,
refusal cause, session error, socket or listener.

Every error boundary becomes readable. The document provides dioxus-core's own boundary factory at its root scope
before the first build, so every boundary registers its `ErrorContext` there: the root one and each of the app's own.
P3 measured both. A panic's location comes from a chaining panic hook that escher-telemetry's capture installs once
per process. It is inert unless a capture is open on the panicking thread (the operator's answer at P4, below).

2. **Every boundary readable** — `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/boundary.rs`, `dioxus_document.rs`, `lib.rs`.
   - **The factory.** An ungated `BoundaryRegistry` (an `Rc<RefCell<Vec<ErrorContext>>>`) and a plain `fn` factory
     that makes an `ErrorContext::new(None)` and registers it in the registry it consumes from context.
   - **Where it is provided.** `DioxusDocument::new` provides both at `ScopeId::ROOT` through `vdom.in_scope`,
     before the first build, as P3 measured.
   - **The marks.** `DioxusDocument::boundary_marks()` returns one mark per registered boundary holding an error,
     compared by `Arc::ptr_eq`. `RootErrorMark` stays as it is. Where the root boundary is not among the registered
     ones (a document built after its vdom's first build), the root one is read through `ROOT_ERROR_BOUNDARY` as
     today.
   - **The read.** A mark reads as a `BoundaryError { boundary: Root | Own, message, chain }`: the message is the
     error's top line (`to_string`), the chain each `anyhow` source after it in order. It reads nothing else and logs
     nothing.
   - Unit tests in `boundary.rs`'s module:
     - a root `Err` reads `Root` with its chain;
     - an `Err` under an `ErrorBoundary` of the app's own reads `Own` with its three-link chain, and the root holds
       none;
     - a second step leaves the first error's mark unchanged;
     - with two contexts registered for one own boundary (the root's and the app's, as measured), each error is read
       once.

4. **The written form and the help** — `packages/escher-driver/src/json.rs`, `schema.rs`, `schema_tests.rs`,
   `explore.rs`.
   - **The writer.** `caused_item` writes the members in step 3's order, each present only where it holds:
     - `cut` only on a cut text;
     - `chain` only on an error;
     - `fields` and `fields_past` only on a log record.
     The acting answers write `caused_past` after `caused`, only when non-empty, as
     `[{"kind","source","count"}]`. The string escaping stands (arch · contract/answer-json/string-escaping), so a
     newline or an ESC byte in a message is written escaped and the line stays one uncoloured line.
   - **The help.** `CAUSED`'s help is rewritten in the program's own fixed text (arch ·
     decision/fixed-program-text-on-carriers). It names:
     - each member, the closed `source` and `boundary` words, the cut's meaning, the 16-item count and `caused_past`;
     - the scrub: content-named fields and an engine record's message shown as `[redacted]`;
     - the stated limits: a `log` crate record read only where the process's telemetry bridged it; an app that
       provides its own boundary factory shadows the document's; a location as the compiler wrote it, a dependency's
       an absolute path; a record from the app's own code holds what the app wrote into its message.
   - **The new field.** A `CAUSED_PAST` field spec joins the five acting verbs after `CAUSED`.
   - `schema_tests.rs` and `json.rs`' unit tables move to the new shape, every member written and absent where it
     must be, rows counted.

5. **The standing check follows the new contract** — `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_errors.rs`.
   - Its items compare against the per-record shape: the log button's two records are two items, the input's two
     debug records two items.
   - Its `holds_no_sentinel` assertions over the answer, the MCP result and the kept check turn into assertions that
     each sentinel IS in `caused`.
   - Its `command`-span case keeps asserting that no sentinel and no `caused` reaches a span field.
   - The root `Err` case reads the error's text in `caused`, `boundary` `root`, beside the boundary's screen
     rendering.
   - Its `//!` doc is restated.

7. **The hook installs once and changes nothing outside a capture** — `tests/blitz-tests/tests/capture_panic_hook.rs`
   (new, one behaviour, one `#[test]` so no other test's panic races it; the operator's note at P4). It installs a
   counting hook, opens a capture once, then panics outside any capture:
   - the counting hook runs exactly once for that panic and nothing is captured;
   - a panic inside a capture is captured with its payload and location, and the counting hook runs for it too;
   - a second and a third `capture` install no further hook — the counting hook still runs once per panic, never
     twice.
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_error_text.rs` — the founder's question on a real-failure fixture, every carrier, both modes
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/capture_panic_hook.rs` — the capture's hook installs once and leaves a panic outside a capture as it was
- `packages/escher-telemetry/src/capture.rs` — the capture keeps scrubbed, cut text records and panics; the chaining hook
- `packages/escher-telemetry/src/format.rs` — the field rule callable by the capture
- `packages/escher-telemetry/src/lib.rs` — re-exports of the capture's new types
- `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/boundary.rs` — the boundary registry, factory, marks and reader
- `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/dioxus_document.rs` — the factory provided at the root scope at construction
- `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/lib.rs` — re-exports
- `packages/escher-driver/src/caused.rs` — the per-record item, the order, the count and `CausedPast`
- `packages/escher-driver/src/execute.rs` — the boundary marks before the step; `caused_past` on the acting outcomes
- `packages/escher-driver/src/json.rs` — the item's members and `caused_past` written by hand; its unit tables
- `packages/escher-driver/src/schema.rs` — `CAUSED`'s help and the `CAUSED_PAST` field
- `packages/escher-driver/src/schema_tests.rs` — the field and help pins
- `packages/escher-driver/src/explore.rs` — the panicked ending read off the reshaped item
- `packages/escher-driver/src/lib.rs` — re-exports
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_errors.rs` — the standing check moved to the text-carrying contract
The gates are:
- the three crates' unit tests;
- the two new targets and the moved standing check, in both layout modes;

- escher-telemetry's process checks (`telemetry_scrub`, `telemetry_drop`, `telemetry_panic_hook`), which show that
  the sink prints what it printed;
- seven_guis' `host_log` and `mcp_log`, at trace with 0 needles;
- then the pre-push gate, `stand-repeat` (which `stand_act_error_text` joins by its prefix) and the coverage leg.

No boot-path touchpoint changes a binary's start. `host_log` and `mcp_log` drive both binaries' roles under the
changed capture, and stand in for the smoke. No live leg.

Each new check is controlled red-before-green (tests S4). After the steps are green, /implement runs four one-shot
`gate.py control` runs, never entries:
- The scrub's content-name test made always-false in `capture.rs`: `stand_act_error_text`'s scrub case reads failed.

- `TEXT_CUT` loosened to 2048 in `capture.rs`: the flood case reads failed. It is loosened, not removed, so the run
  stays bounded.
- The chaining hook's call to the replaced hook removed: `capture_panic_hook`'s case reads failed.

- The factory's provision in `DioxusDocument::new` removed: the own-boundary case of `stand_act_error_text` reads
  failed.
Each control names the edit's text and the case by its test name (gate-contract.md §Control).

The diff is OS-sensitive in one place: a panic's location file is the compiler's spelling, `\` on Windows. The check
compares it with the fixture's own `file!()`, never a literal. The socket carrier case is unix-gated. The operator's
hygiene, push and CI entries stand for that, and because the workspace leg builds the engine with `tracing` on (test-plan
· decision/per-package-green-not-workspace-green).

body:
- (founder) On the real-failure fixture, in both layout modes, an agent reading the acting answer alone can say what
  failed and where. Each failing click's written line carries values, not only keys:
  - the panic's payload and its location (the fixture's file, the failing line);
  - the `Err`'s top line, its whole three-link chain in order and the boundary that took it — the root one, or the
    app's own;
  - the handler's id and event.
  `cargo test -p blitz-tests --locked --test stand_act_error_text` returns 0 (inputs#I1, point 5).

- (security) The scrub hides by field name alone. A `password` and a `value` field read `[redacted]` by name, while
  the message and the other fields cross whole. An engine record's message reads `[redacted]` (the sink's own rule).
  A typed password occurs 0 times in the answer, its snapshot value `MASKED_VALUE` (security ·
  decision/mask-holds-on-every-carrier).

- (bounds) A text past 1024 bytes arrives cut, with `cut` its bytes cut. An answer holds at most 16 items, the rest
  counted in `caused_past` by kind and source. The flood fixture's whole line is under 1,048,576 bytes (arch ·
  contract/mcp-stdio/result, contract/session-socket-wire/answer-bound).

- (carriers) The same `caused` crosses `Session::run`, `serve_mcp`, the session socket (unix) and a kept check that
  replays holding; a changed copy stops naming `caused`.

- (obs) Under escher's own sink at `trace` the failing steps' sentinels and payloads occur 0 times on the sink's
  lines. The `command` span keeps its eight fields, holding no `caused`.
  `cargo test -p seven_guis --locked --test host_log --test mcp_log` returns 0 (obs ·
  decision/driver-span-fields-print, security · decision/no-screen-content-in-logs).

- (hook) A panic outside any capture runs the hook it replaced exactly once and captures nothing. The hook is
  installed once per process: `cargo test -p blitz-tests --locked --test capture_panic_hook` returns 0 (the
  operator's note at P4).

- (no move) `stand_cross_os_readings`' committed digests are unchanged and `stand_replay`'s committed Counter checks
  replay holding.

- (tests) `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh fast`, `stand-repeat` and `coverage` are green, and the operator pass's CI
  read reads `verdict: green`.

- No capability is claimed. The pool's three (v030-11, v030-12, v030-15) belong to «Layout on the carriers», «A
  component in isolation» and «Cold-agent bar».

- inputs#I1 — the founder's answer, his purpose and the five points he confirmed: the content, the scrub, the
  measured bound, the said cut, the counted rest, where-and-which-source-and-chain, and the acceptance's question.

- The P4 answer: the operator chose «Capture's chaining hook (Recommended)» for the panic's location (2026-11-16,

  prints exactly as before, and one that the hook installs once per process — step 7.

- Rows: arch · contract/acting-verb-results/caused, decision/capture-dispatcher-pair, decision/capture-before-own-recorder,
  decision/driver-library-side-effect-free, decision/fixed-program-text-on-carriers, contract/answer-json/string-escaping,
  contract/telemetry-scrub/engine-targets; security · decision/caused-answer-crossing,
  decision/root-boundary-err-as-screen-content, decision/boundary-widening-rule, decision/mask-holds-on-every-carrier,
  decision/no-screen-content-in-logs; obs · decision/capture-framework-targets-warn-up, decision/sink-target-allowlist,
  contract/telemetry-scrub-set/error; test-plan · decision/root-boundary-err-on-own-session,
  decision/per-package-green-not-workspace-green, decision/mutation-controlled-tests.

- Research: `doc:2026-11-16-error-text-in-the-answer/research` — the measurement (probe logs at
  `.andromeda/cache/chunks/2026-11-16-error-text-in-the-answer/evidence/`), the boundary factory, the graph impact.

- **A value-based scrub** — a message searched for a masked control's value and blanked. Rejected: the founder's
  point that «the scrub hides a value by its field's name and nothing else» (inputs#I1).

- **Escher's own targets in `caused`** — rejected: the binaries' panic event (`escher_telemetry::panic`) would answer
  each panic twice, and the driver's spans are never content.

- **A seventh served task to drive a failure through the binary** — rejected: the six-task rows (layouts ·
  contract/escher-session-served-tasks/*) stand. The socket carrier is proven through a host child of the test
  binary.

- **A path rewrite of a dependency's absolute location** — rejected for the same «field name and nothing else» reason.
  It is stated in the help as a limit.

- **Never** read a message into a log line, a span field or a `Debug`-printed type (obs ·
  decision/debug-types-never-logged).

- A framework or engine record at `warn` and above cannot be reached on a package-alone build. P3 measured 0 such

  fixture's real failures are the panic, the `Err` chain and the app's own records.

title: The engine's `warn` and `error` sites (the operator's review at P5)

data.head: ## The engine's `warn` and `error` sites (the operator's review at P5)

body:
Enumerated by `git grep -n -A3 -E 'warn!|error!' -- packages/ ':!packages/escher-telemetry' ':!packages/escher-driver'`:
47 hits. 3 are `compile_error!` (accesskit_xplat ×2, dioxus-native's renderer) and 1 is a doc comment
(blitz-vibey-script `document.rs:258`), which leaves **43 sites**. `stylo_taffy` and `debug_timer` hold none.
**Interpolating an attribute value or text — 6 sites in 5 files, each edited:**
| site | interpolates | becomes |
| `blitz-dom/src/events/pointer.rs:1144` | the link's `href` attribute and the document's URL (`Debug`, 205 B measured) | fixed message; fields `href`, `url` |
| `blitz-dom/src/form.rs:156` | the scheme of the form's `action` attribute | fixed message naming the method (a closed enum); field `url` |
| `blitz-dom/src/mutator.rs:1542` | the iframe's raw `src` attribute | fixed message; field `src` |
| `blitz-dom/src/layout/mod.rs:248` | a text node's data, in a field named `data` the scrub does not hide | field renamed `text` |
| `dioxus-native/src/assets.rs:53` | the asset request (`Debug`: its URL) | fixed message; field `request` |
| `dioxus-native/src/assets.rs:60` | the same | the same |
**Interpolating nothing of a page or of typed input — 37 sites, no change:**
- **The shell's winit-variant `Debug` (6):** blitz-shell `convert_events.rs` ×5, `window.rs:852`.

Node ids may cross (the operator's review). Under escher's own sink nothing changes: an engine target still prints
its safe fields alone and its message `[redacted]`. The moved values land in fields the sink redacts by their names
(`href`, `url`, `src`, `text`, `request`).

**Reached on a fixture (a temporary probe, removed after its reading;
`{work_dir}/evidence/probe-reach-{tracing,package}.log`):**

- **Engine, workspace build.** A click on a block link with `href="http://[::1"` reaches `pointer.rs:1144`: a `WARN`
  at `blitz_dom::events::pointer`, 205 B, the raw `href` and the document URL in its message. An invalid inline style
  value (`color: notacolour`) reaches `node/element.rs:821`: a `WARN` at `blitz_dom::node::element`, its message fixed
  (22 B), its fields `property` and `value`. Neither appears in the package-alone build (the engine's `tracing` off).

- **Framework, both builds.** A component whose render returns `Err` (`"seven".parse()?`) reaches dioxus-core
  `scope_arena.rs:111`: an `ERROR` at `dioxus_core::scope_arena`, 99 B, «Error while rendering component `…`: invalid
  digit found in string». Its location is the registry's absolute path.

- **Fixture trap.** A link left inline has no box for `Harness::click` to aim at, and the click lands elsewhere — the
  testing rule's inline-element trap, met once in this probe.
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/events/pointer.rs` — the unparseable-link warning's `href` and URL moved into fields
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/form.rs` — the unimplemented-scheme warning's scheme moved into a field
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/mutator.rs` — the unresolvable-iframe warning's `src` moved into a field
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/layout/mod.rs` — the text-node error's `data` field renamed `text`
- `packages/dioxus-native/src/assets.rs` — the two asset-fetch warnings' request moved into a field
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/lib.rs` — a documented `pub const TRACING_COMPILED: bool`, whether this build compiled the engine's log sites, so a check asserts the engine case per build
- `format.rs`: no change — the capture reads the sink's existing `CONTENT_FIELDS` and `REDACTED` for every source; the sink's own engine rule (safe fields alone, message hidden) stays the sink's.

- the engine's `warn!|error!` sites over `git grep` of `packages/` (escher's crates excluded): 47 hits · 6 changed · 41 no-change (3 `compile_error!`, 1 doc comment, 37 classified in §The engine's sites).

- An acting answer's `caused` (`click` · `type` · `press` · `advance` · `scroll`; `packages/escher-driver/src/caused.rs`,
  built by 2026-11-16-errors-with-the-action as closed words, ids and counts alone) gains the TEXT of what the step
  caused, per record, from every source:
  - a **panic**: its payload and its source location (file, line, column), as the panic hook already reads them
    (`packages/escher-telemetry/src/panic.rs`);
  - an **error** the app's root error boundary took: its message AND its cause chain (each `source()` in turn), not
    its top line alone — today `RootErrorMark` (`packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/boundary.rs`) holds the error by
    identity and reads nothing of it;
  - a **log record** from the app, the UI framework and the engine: its message, its target (which source said it),
    its level, the location a bridged `log` record carries (`log.file` · `log.line`) and its fields — today the
    capture (`packages/escher-telemetry/src/capture.rs`) counts records by level alone and admits no engine or escher
    target. [the operator's direction at the P5 review, 2026-11-16: an engine record at `warn` and above crosses with
    its message as text, as an app's and the framework's do, every source's content-named fields hidden by name. The
    engine's `warn` and `error` sites are enumerated (43). Each one that interpolates an attribute value or text into
    its message has that value moved into a named field the scrub hides — 6 sites in 5 files of blitz-dom and
    dioxus-native, a direct edit of the engine code (`doc:2026-11-16-error-text-in-the-answer/research` §The
    engine's sites). Node ids may cross. The sink's own engine rule is unchanged on its log lines.]

- On a fixture with a **real failure** (a handler that fails the way an app fails — a panic in a real code path, an
  `Err` with a cause chain, a framework or engine record), an agent reading **the answer alone** can say what failed
  and where: the acceptance asserts the message, the source location and the cause chain are in the answer, not only
  that the fields are present. [measured after the operator's P5 review: no stand step causes a framework or engine
  record at `warn` or above (39 steps, both builds), but a fixture reaches one of each. A framework `ERROR` at
  `dioxus_core::scope_arena` comes from a component whose render returns `Err`, under both builds. An engine `WARN`
  at `blitz_dom::events::pointer` comes from a click on a link whose `href` will not parse, under the workspace
  build, where the engine's `tracing` is compiled; under the package-alone build it is absent, and the check states
  which build it read.]

- **Marker:** 2026-11-16-error-text-in-the-answer · **Version:** escher-0.3.0 · **Generated:** 2026-11-16T18:15:25Z
  (re-synthesised after the operator's P5 review)

It does this for every source: the app at every level, and the UI framework and the engine at `warn` and above. Every
message crosses as text, the engine's included. Every source's content-named fields are hidden by name, and nothing
else is (inputs#I1, the operator's P5 review). Each text is cut at a fixed length that says how much it cut. An
answer holds a fixed count of items, and the rest are counted by kind and source (inputs#I1: «Скраб и граница
(Recommended)» and its five confirmed points).

The engine's `warn` and `error` sites were enumerated: 43. The 6 that interpolated an attribute value or text into
their message now carry that value in a named field the scrub hides — a direct edit of blitz-dom and dioxus-native.
Node ids may cross.

- **Cut:** 1024 bytes per text. The longest admitted message measured was 205 B: the engine's unparseable-link
  warning, before its edit.

Every error boundary becomes readable. The document provides dioxus-core's own boundary factory at its root scope
before the first build, so every boundary registers its `ErrorContext` there: the root one and each of the app's own.
P3 measured both. A panic's location comes from a chaining panic hook that escher-telemetry's capture installs once
per process. It is inert unless a capture is open on the panicking thread (the operator's answer at P4).

2. **The engine's interpolating sites carry the value in a hidden field** — a direct edit of the engine code, the
   operator's direction at the P5 review. Each message becomes fixed text naming what failed, and each value moves
   into a field named in `CONTENT_FIELDS`. The sites are research's table, re-read at HEAD before editing:
   - `packages/blitz-dom/src/events/pointer.rs` (the unparseable link): the raw `href` into `href`, the document URL
     into `url`;
   - `packages/blitz-dom/src/form.rs` (the unimplemented form scheme): the scheme into `url`, the method (a closed
     enum) staying in the message;
   - `packages/blitz-dom/src/mutator.rs` (the unresolvable iframe): the raw `src` into `src`;
   - `packages/blitz-dom/src/layout/mod.rs` (a text node laid out alone): its `data` field renamed `text`;
   - `packages/dioxus-native/src/assets.rs`, both asset-fetch warnings: the request into `request`.
   The level, target and `#[cfg(feature = "tracing")]` gating of each site stay as they are. Each change is flagged
   upstreamable (arch · decision/direct-engine-changes-flagged-upstreamable).
   - `packages/blitz-dom/src/lib.rs` gains a documented `pub const TRACING_COMPILED: bool = cfg!(feature =
     "tracing")`, so a check asserts the engine case under the build it runs in.

3. **Every boundary readable** — `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/boundary.rs`, `dioxus_document.rs`, `lib.rs`.
   - **The factory.** An ungated `BoundaryRegistry` (an `Rc<RefCell<Vec<ErrorContext>>>`) and a plain `fn` factory
     that makes an `ErrorContext::new(None)` and registers it in the registry it consumes from context.
   - **Where it is provided.** `DioxusDocument::new` provides both at `ScopeId::ROOT` through `vdom.in_scope`,
     before the first build, as P3 measured.
   - **The marks.** `DioxusDocument::boundary_marks()` returns one mark per registered boundary holding an error,
     compared by `Arc::ptr_eq`. `RootErrorMark` stays as it is. Where the root boundary is not among the registered
     ones (a document built after its vdom's first build), the root one is read through `ROOT_ERROR_BOUNDARY` as
     today.
   - **The read.** A mark reads as a `BoundaryError { boundary: Root | Own, message, chain }`: the message is the
     error's top line (`to_string`), the chain each `anyhow` source after it in order. It reads nothing else and logs
     nothing.
   - Unit tests in `boundary.rs`'s module:
     - a root `Err` reads `Root` with its chain;
     - an `Err` under an `ErrorBoundary` of the app's own reads `Own` with its three-link chain, and the root holds
       none;
     - a second step leaves the first error's mark unchanged;
     - with two contexts registered for one own boundary (the root's and the app's, as measured), each error is read
       once.

5. **The written form and the help** — `packages/escher-driver/src/json.rs`, `schema.rs`, `schema_tests.rs`,
   `explore.rs`.
   - **The writer.** `caused_item` writes the members in step 4's order, each present only where it holds:
     - `cut` only on a cut text;
     - `chain` only on an error;
     - `fields` and `fields_past` only on a log record.
     The acting answers write `caused_past` after `caused`, only when non-empty, as
     `[{"kind","source","count"}]`. The string escaping stands (arch · contract/answer-json/string-escaping), so a
     newline or an ESC byte in a message is written escaped and the line stays one uncoloured line.
   - **The help.** `CAUSED`'s help is rewritten in the program's own fixed text (arch ·
     decision/fixed-program-text-on-carriers). It names:
     - each member, the closed `source` and `boundary` words, the cut's meaning, the 16-item count and `caused_past`;
     - the scrub: content-named fields shown as `[redacted]`, every message crossing;
     - the stated limits: an engine record exists only in a build that compiled the engine's `tracing`; a `log` crate
       record is read only where the process's telemetry bridged it; an app that provides its own boundary factory
       shadows the document's; a location is as the compiler wrote it, a dependency's an absolute path; a message
       holds what its author wrote into it.
   - **The new field.** A `CAUSED_PAST` field spec joins the five acting verbs after `CAUSED`.
   - `schema_tests.rs` and `json.rs`' unit tables move to the new shape, every member written and absent where it
     must be, rows counted.

6. **The standing check follows the new contract** — `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_errors.rs`.
   - Its items compare against the per-record shape: the log button's two records are two items, the input's two
     debug records two items.
   - Its `holds_no_sentinel` assertions over the answer, the MCP result and the kept check turn into assertions that
     each sentinel IS in `caused`.
   - Its `command`-span case keeps asserting that no sentinel and no `caused` reaches a span field.
   - The root `Err` case reads the error's text in `caused`, `boundary` `root`, beside the boundary's screen
     rendering.
   - Its `//!` doc is restated.

8. **The hook installs once and changes nothing outside a capture** — `tests/blitz-tests/tests/capture_panic_hook.rs`
   (new, one behaviour, one `#[test]` so no other test's panic races it; the operator's note at P4). It installs a
   counting hook, opens a capture once, then panics outside any capture:
   - the counting hook runs exactly once for that panic and nothing is captured;
   - a panic inside a capture is captured with its payload and location, and the counting hook runs for it too;
   - a second and a third `capture` install no further hook — the counting hook still runs once per panic, never
     twice.
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_error_text.rs` — the founder's question on real failures of every source, every carrier, both modes, both builds
- `packages/escher-telemetry/src/format.rs` — the field rule callable by the capture
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/events/pointer.rs` — the unparseable-link warning's `href` and URL moved into fields
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/form.rs` — the unimplemented-scheme warning's scheme moved into a field
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/mutator.rs` — the unresolvable-iframe warning's `src` moved into a field
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/layout/mod.rs` — the text-node error's `data` field renamed `text`
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/lib.rs` — `TRACING_COMPILED`
- `packages/dioxus-native/src/assets.rs` — the two asset-fetch warnings' request moved into a field

- escher-telemetry's process checks (`telemetry_scrub`, `telemetry_drop`, `telemetry_panic_hook`), which show that
  the sink prints what it printed, the moved engine values now `[redacted]` fields;

- then the pre-push gate, `stand-repeat` (which `stand_act_error_text` joins by its prefix, per package) and the
  coverage leg.

Each new check is controlled red-before-green (tests S4). After the steps are green, /implement runs five one-shot
`gate.py control` runs, never entries:

- The factory's provision in `DioxusDocument::new` removed: the own-boundary case of `stand_act_error_text` reads
  failed.
- The `href` interpolation restored in `pointer.rs`'s message: the engine case reads failed under the tracing entry.

The diff is OS-sensitive in one place: a panic's location file is the compiler's spelling, `\` on Windows. The check
compares it with the fixture's own `file!()`, never a literal. The socket carrier case is unix-gated. The operator's

- (security) The scrub hides by field name alone, the same rule for every source. A `password` and a `value` field
  read `[redacted]` by name, and so do the engine's moved `href`, `url` and `value`, while every message — the
  engine's included — and the other fields cross whole. A typed password and the raw `href` occur 0 times in the
  answer, the password's snapshot value `MASKED_VALUE` (security · decision/mask-holds-on-every-carrier).

- (engine) Of the 43 engine `warn` and `error` sites, the 6 that interpolated an attribute value or text carry it in
  a field named in `CONTENT_FIELDS`, and their message is fixed text: `git grep` of research's six sites reads the
  fields, and the founder's target reads the link site's message whole and its fields hidden.

- (obs) Under escher's own sink at `trace` the failing steps' sentinels, payloads and the raw `href` occur 0 times on
  the sink's lines. The `command` span keeps its eight fields, holding no `caused`.
  `cargo test -p seven_guis --locked --test host_log --test mcp_log` returns 0 (obs ·
  decision/driver-span-fields-print, security · decision/no-screen-content-in-logs).

- The P4 answer: the operator chose «Capture's chaining hook (Recommended)» for the panic's location (2026-11-16,
  AskUserQuestion in this session), with the note that the plan carries a check that a panic with no capture open
  prints exactly as before, and one that the hook installs once per process — step 8.

- Rows: arch · contract/acting-verb-results/caused, decision/capture-dispatcher-pair, decision/capture-before-own-recorder,
  decision/driver-library-side-effect-free, decision/fixed-program-text-on-carriers, contract/answer-json/string-escaping,
  contract/telemetry-scrub/engine-targets, decision/direct-engine-changes-flagged-upstreamable; security ·
  decision/caused-answer-crossing, decision/root-boundary-err-as-screen-content, decision/boundary-widening-rule,
  decision/mask-holds-on-every-carrier, decision/no-screen-content-in-logs, decision/engine-target-safe-fields; obs ·
  decision/capture-framework-targets-warn-up, decision/sink-target-allowlist, contract/telemetry-scrub-set/error;
  test-plan · decision/root-boundary-err-on-own-session, decision/per-package-green-not-workspace-green,
  decision/mutation-controlled-tests.

- Research: `doc:2026-11-16-error-text-in-the-answer/research` — the measurement, the engine's sites and their
  reach, the boundary factory, the graph impact (probe logs at
  `.andromeda/cache/chunks/2026-11-16-error-text-in-the-answer/evidence/`).

- **An engine record's message hidden** (the sink's own engine rule applied to the answer) — rejected at the
  operator's P5 review: the founder asked for every error's context, and a message is not blanked because one field
  in it is. The interpolated values move into hidden fields instead (step 2).

- **Engine and framework records below `warn`** — rejected on the measurement:
  - they cross every step (one engine record per focus move, the framework's traces up to 4106 B);
  - they exist, for the engine, under the workspace build alone, so the stand's acting answers would differ by build
    and `stand_cross_os_readings`' digests with them.

- **A blitz-tests feature forwarding `dioxus-native-dom/tracing`** — rejected: Cargo does not let a package's features
  enable a dev-dependency's. `TRACING_COMPILED` tells the check which build it runs in.

- **The engine sites.** Research's table names each one with its line at the rows' pin, and implement re-reads each
  site at HEAD before editing. The 37 left unchanged hold fixed messages, closed values, the shell's winit variants,
  or the failure's own error text (html5ever's fixed strings with `exact_errors: false`, a script's uncaught error,
  an io error).

- **The bad link.** P3's reach probe measured the engine's unparseable-link warning at 205 B, holding the raw `href`
  and the document URL's `Debug`. After step 2 it holds neither.

- **Inline elements.** A clicked link must be a block box with a size: a click aimed at an inline element misses —
  measured once in the reach probe, and the testing rule's trap.

- **Framework records.** The framework's render error is reached under both builds (`dioxus_core` compiles its
  `tracing` unconditionally), its location the registry's absolute path. The fixture mounts it under the app's own
  boundary, so the app stays on screen for the following steps.

- **Two contexts per own boundary.** With the factory provided before the first build, P3 read 2 contexts registered
  at boot for an app with one own boundary: the root error boundary's and the app's. Step 3's reader must read each
  error once.

- **Shadowed boundaries.** An app that provides its own boundary factory (fullstack's hydration factory) shadows the
  document's for the scopes under it. Stated in the help, never silent.

- **Third-party crates.** A record from a crate outside the three prefix sets (Stylo's `style`, Parley, html5ever's
  own) is classed `app`, as the capture classes it today. No stand step caused one at `warn` or above under either
  build. This is stated in the help as the source word's limit.

**Date:** 2026-11-16
**Run:** 2026-11-16T18-24-23-implement

- **Symbols / APIs:**
  - escher-telemetry `capture`: the capture keeps text. New public `Source` (`App` · `Framework` · `Engine`, `name()` → `app` · `framework` · `engine`, `ALL`), `Text { text, cut }` with `Text::cut`, `KeptField { name, value }`, `Record { source, target, level, message, fields, fields_past, file, line }`, `Panic { payload, file, line, column }`; constants `TEXT_CUT` = 1024, `FIELDS_KEPT` = 8, `RECORDS_KEPT` = 16. `Captured` gains `records()`, `records_past(Source)`, `panics()`, `panics_past()`; it is no longer `Copy`; `is_empty()` also reads panics; its `Debug` prints the level counts alone. The admission rule: an app target (outside the three prefix sets) at every level, framework (`FRAMEWORK_TARGET_PREFIXES`) and engine (`ENGINE_TARGET_PREFIXES`) at `warn`/`error`, an `escher_` target never — the engine at `warn` and above is NEW (it was never counted). `log.*` bridge fields are left out of a record's fields. `capture()` now installs, once per process (`std::sync::Once`), a chaining panic hook: on a panic it keeps the payload and location on the capture open on the panicking thread (none open: nothing), then always runs the hook it replaced; it prints, logs and fields nothing. Each of `Text`, `KeptField`, `Record`, `Panic` has a hand `Debug` printing no text.
  - escher-telemetry `lib`: `pub fn subscriber(identity, writer, level: LevelFilter)` — the sink's subscriber plus `CaptureLayer`, built uninstalled (was a private fn taking `EnvFilter`; the private one is `filtered_subscriber`, used by `init_with_writer`). Callers: `init_with_writer` (private path), capture's unit test, `stand_act_error_text`.
  - escher-telemetry `format`: `CONTENT_FIELDS` gains `password` (12 names).
  - blitz-dom: `pub const TRACING_COMPILED: bool = cfg!(feature = "tracing")` in `lib.rs`.

Ungated by any feature.
  - escher-driver `caused`: `Caused` is one item per record — `kind`, `level`, `source: Option<Source>`, `target`, `message: Text`, `file`, `line`, `column`, `boundary: Option<Boundary>`, `chain: Vec<Text>`, `chain_past`, `fields: Vec<KeptField>`, `fields_past`, `id`, `owner`, `event`; `count` removed. New `CausedPast { kind, source, count }`, constants `CAUSED_KEPT` = 16, `CHAIN_KEPT` = 8, fn `boundary_word` (`root` · `own`). Order: panics, errors new since the step's marks (every boundary's), then records in record order; first 16 kept, rest counted by kind and source; a caught panic the hook did not see answers an item with message `<payload unread>`.

title: I6-error-field-founder-2026-11-16.md.txt
body:
# The founder's answers at the wrap of «Error text in the answer» — 2026-11-16

The founder answered two questions by question dialog in the overseer session on 2026-11-16; the answers were read at
21:06Z. Both are his own chosen labels, verbatim; the overseer relays them.

## 1. The wrap's widening card — 14 master operations

> «Применить все 14 (Recommended)»

The option as it was read to him: the masters (architecture, security-plan, obs-plan, test-plan) are brought to the
built code and to his answer of the same day («Скраб и граница (Recommended)»): `caused` carries text; the rules «an
answer echoes nothing typed» and «the mask holds on every carrier» gain a stated exception for an author's own
message; two older decisions on closed words retire and their heirs stand in their place. Its stated price: his word
for a boundary widening — an author's text from the app, the framework and the engine crosses every carrier of an
answer. Passed over: reject all 14 · hold the card.

## 2. The field named `error` in a `caused` item

> «Открыть error в caused (Recommended)»

What he was told: the scrub by field name was taken from the log sink as it stands, and its set holds the name `error`
(with `path`, `text`, `request`, `url`, `href`, `src`); a usual Rust record of a failure keeps the error's text in a
field of that name, so an agent reads `[redacted]` in its place; a panic's and an `Err`'s message and cause chain
cross whole — what is lost is the `error` field of a log record.

The option as it was read to him: a small chunk of its own, next — the answer to an agent has its own scrub set,
without `error` (the error's text is shown), the other names staying hidden; the log sink's stderr lines do not
change. Its stated price: the error's text can hold what its author put into it (a failed fetch's URL inside the
error text — the reason `error` was in the set); one more chunk and one more widening card at its wrap.

Passed over, as they were read to him:
- open `error`, `path` and the URL fields (`url`, `href`, `src`, `request`) — wider, a URL's query can carry a token;
- leave the set as it is, one for the sink and the answer.

- The target allowlist and the scrub live in `format.rs`, three outcomes by target (a bridged record judged by its `log.target`): a target starting with a prefix in `ENGINE_TARGET_PREFIXES` (`blitz` · `dioxus_native` · `stylo_taffy` · `accesskit_xplat` · `debug_timer` · `js_console`) prints only `SAFE_FIELDS` (`node_id` · `status` · `waiting_nodes` · `property` · `log.module_path` · `log.file` · `log.line`), every other field — the message included — as `{name}=[redacted]`; a target starting with a prefix in `ESCHER_TARGET_PREFIXES` (`escher_`, the underscore part of the prefix) prints every field not in `CONTENT_FIELDS` (`url` · `href` · `src` · `html` · `text` · `value` · `attrs` · `path` · `request` · `error` · `password` · `panic.payload`), those redacted; a target starting with a prefix of neither set is dropped whole — zero bytes, at every level, WARN and ERROR included, whatever `RUST_LOG` names. Engine and framework warn and error sites write fixed messages and carry their values in named fields (`href` · `url` · `src` · `text` · `request`), so the field-name scrub reaches them; no filter layer is added: the drop sits in the formatter.

- Process-global: a second `init` changes nothing (`AlreadyInstalled`), and another global subscriber or `log` logger makes it `ForeignSubscriber`. The first install is recorded in a static `OnceLock<ServiceIdentity>` behind a static `Mutex<()>`; it spawns no thread. The capture installs once per process a chaining panic hook that keeps a panic's payload and location on the open capture, prints and logs nothing, and always runs the hook it replaced. Where the held default has no capture layer, the log capture uses a process-wide pair of scoped dispatchers built once and never dropped, one used and a twin never used, so tracing-core never falls into its one-dispatcher interest mode.
